items.heading: Pharmacy Is a Real, Licensed,
items.text: Pharmacy Is a Real, Licensed, Pharmacy is a real, licensed, regulated profession in India under the Pharmacy Council of India, not a dressed-up retail job with no ceiling.

items.heading: "Pharmacist Salary in India"
items.text: "Pharmacist salary in India" is close to a meaningless single number, because the spread between an unorganised independent-store counter role and a specialised hospital or export-facing job is enormous, and most college marketing quotes only the flattering end of it.

visuals.heading: The Real Pay Behind the Brochure

rows: Rarely crosses ₹60,000-70,000/month without adding a B.Pharm or M.Pharm on top, this is the true entry floor, not the exception.
Roughly ₹2.5-4 lakh/year at a branded chain (e.g. Apollo Pharmacy); lower at an independent store
Branded-chain pay is the better end of retail. A large share of India's roughly 8.5 lakh pharmacy outlets are small, unorganised stores paying below this.
Roughly ₹4-8 lakh/year; ICU or oncology clinical-pharmacy roles at large hospitals can reach ₹8-14 lakh/year
The stronger employed-pharmacist tier, but it usually needs a B.Pharm or Pharm.D plus a specific hospital's hiring bar, not just a licence.
Roughly ₹15,900/month (about ₹1.9 lakh/year) per aggregated 2026 salary-tracker data
This blended figure sits well below the headline ranges brochures quote, because it averages in the large unorganised-retail majority.

items.heading: Between 2016
items.text: Between 2016-17 and 2025-26, the number of colleges offering B.Pharm courses in Maharashtra alone tripled, from 168 to 531, while cumulative intake more than quadrupled, expansion that outpaced genuine student interest, not demand from employers.

items.heading: After the Final Admission Round
items.text: After the final admission round for 2025-26, roughly 15,936 B.Pharm seats and 815 M.Pharm seats stayed vacant in Maharashtra, with more than 32% of B.Pharm seats unfilled despite multiple counselling rounds.

items.heading: "Pharmacy Has Huge Scope"
items.text: "Pharmacy has huge scope" is the line every admission brochure repeats, but a seat sitting empty in a mushrooming college is not the same signal as a hospital or exporter actively short of hires.
